outline.label: Opening salvo + Fig. 1.1 chimpanzee
outline.summary: Darwin's 1872 Expression as continuity-across-species argument; orangutan/chimpanzee lip-protrusion passage (E 139-140) as inseparably rhetorical and scientific; thesis: Darwin foregrounds inherent rhetoricity of emotion, outstripping Ekman; aligns Darwin with situated cognition (Noé).

outline.label: Ekman 1998 introduction + Duchenne photographs (Figs. 1.2-1.4)
outline.summary: Bestseller-decline-revival arc; Ekman's 1998 third-edition commentary; Duchenne galvanism passage (E 21); Ekman's PoFA basic-emotion image set (Fig. 1.5: anger/fear/disgust/surprise/joy/sadness/contempt); FACS infrastructure; Damasio amygdala-trustworthiness Nature paper as exemplar.

outline.label: Noé 'The New Phrenology?' + Kagan critique
outline.summary: Three problems of brain-imaging localization (two-directional feedback, normalizing imperatives, indirect-correlation chains); Kagan: distinct phenomena need distinct metrics; amygdala-photo experiment ≠ emotion; methodological core of chapter.

outline.label: Ekman 'basic emotions' definition + CAL critique
outline.summary: Adaptive-evolutionary definition of 'basic'; disgust as model-emotion; impoverished Darwinian model imported into Cognitive Approaches to Literature (CAL) — Howard, Crane, Thrailkill, Keen — and the diminishing returns of cognitive-approaches readings; Gross's alternative: 'rhetorical model of cognition' situated in brain-body-world nexus.

outline.label: Crane Shakespeare's Brain critique + Berlant compassionate-conservatism political stake
outline.summary: Crane's lexical analysis of home in Comedy of Errors; brain-as-material-site-of-discourse argument fails because all human action is locatable in the brain at some point; Berlant on compassionate conservatism (Compassion intro, 2004) — face-to-face emotional accounts have institutional/political stakes; the brain-world pincer 'hampers cultural work' regardless of politics.

outline.label: Darwin's rhetorical methodology + devotion as historical artifact + maternal love
outline.summary: Word-image relation in Darwin; Darwin's caveat on Duchenne photographs (imagination as misguide, E 21); the omitted-from-Ekman emotions: love, sympathy, hatred, suspicion, envy, jealousy, avarice, revenge, deceit, devotion, slyness, guilt, vanity, conceit, ambition, pride, humility; devotion passage (E 217-218 — kneeling-as-captive, dare manus); civilization as distinct emotional regime contradicting Pleistocene-continuity; maternal love crux (E 82): 'No emotion is stronger than maternal love' yet a mother 'may not show it any outward sign' — complex states of mind not revealed by fixed expression.

outline.label: Shakespeare-Spenser literary citations + Aristotelian hatred passage
outline.summary: Darwin turns to literary humanities: envy 'lean-faced in her loathsome ease', jealousy 'the green-eyed monster' (Shakespeare), suspicion 'foul ill-favoured, and grim' (Spenser) — E 260; Ekman relabels these 'affective commitments' (Commentaries, 83); Darwin's hatred-passage (E 234) as Aristotle-Rhetoric-Book-II analogue: hatred specified through cast-of-characters and uneven social relationships (suffered/expecting/willful injury), with subjective perception 'systematically distorted by hegemonic constructs including racism and patriarchy'.

outline.label: Visual-arts case: Laocoön (Fig. 1.6) + Bell's Anatomy (Fig. 1.7)
outline.summary: First-century Laocoön sculpture variously read — Virgil mugitus 'bellowing', Winckelmann edle 'noble', Lessing 'groaning', Charles Bell 'silently struggling'; Bell's Anatomy and Philosophy of Expression as Connected with the Fine Arts as Darwin's polemical foil (E 436n16); Lessing's argument that visual arts must disperse violent emotions; necessary but insufficient — the 'skillfully given accessories' (sea serpent, two sons, off-stage vengeful Apollo, doomed Trojans) make the emotional reading possible.

outline.label: Happy Meal countermodel + Fig. 1.8 joystick + Marx-by-association
outline.summary: McDonald's Happy Meal (Fig. 1.8 center) as efficient countermodel to Ekman pseudo-Darwinianism: not an emotionally competent object triggering happy faces but a 'social transaction' artifact; Gross 'heretically' imagines Darwin turning toward Marx — accessory has 'taken on a life of its own' (commodity-fetish reading); Chalmers Foreword to Clark Supersizing the Mind on 'extended emotions'; Noé 'In the Beginning Was the Situation'; Dreyfus on emotional settings as needed for AI.

outline.label: Sterne A Sentimental Journey: peasants-passage as critical case
outline.summary: Yorick crossing Turin-Savoy mountains; the 'fear not, envied not' apostrophe to peasants (Sterne 120); pathos through distancing mechanisms not face-to-face presence; sentimental-commerce as 'imbalance of social exchange' (9); contrast Pinker 'cheesecake for the mind' literary Darwinism; the classical horror-to-pity sequence restaged critically not virtually; Zunshine theory-of-mind Cartesian computing critique.

outline.label: Negation as rhetorical operator: Sterne + Austen
outline.summary: Negated emotions ('fear not', 'envied not') as load-bearing; Russell's logical 'no not' contra rhetorical function; Austen Emma 'no unhappy reverie' (Harriet, Emma p.321) ≠ logically-equivalent 'happy reverie'; Horn A Natural History of Negation as neo-Gricean masterpiece — litotes (Pope-pseudonym: 'Ladies, Whisperers, and Backbiters', Horn 304); Maxim of Manner violation flags non-stereotypic situation; the 'judge and friend' Emma Woodhouse pair as cultural-stereotype-violation.

outline.label: Background contra Searle/Dreyfus + uncomfortable situatedness
outline.summary: Background-of-intentionality (Searle, Dreyfus): nonrepresentation as afterthought of normal comportment vs. nonrepresentation as flouting-of-conversational-norm in literature (Horn); literature in 'special position to teach us about normality and its construction'; cognition 'practically situated but uncomfortably so' — the volume's titular thesis crystallized; Yorick's pseudo-resolved discomfort produces 'second-order discomfort' in the reader.

outline.label: Roughgarden biodiversity argument + Fig. 1.9 weeping children + closing
outline.summary: Indeterminacy as constitutive not maladaptive; Joan Roughgarden Evolution's Rainbow on 'balanced portfolio' of genes vs. selection-for-ideal-types; semiotic indeterminacy as biodiversity-corollate; Darwin Fig. 1.9 weeping-children plate (Ginx's Baby; cf. Prodger on Rejlander); closing thesis: arts and literature operate at appropriate phenomenological level — people-in-situations, manipulated, ironic, with the 'shimmer just beyond grasp' available through tropes (irony).

concepts.label: rhetoricity of emotion
concepts.gloss: Emotions are constitutively rhetorical — bound to medium, occasion, social situation; rhetoricity is methodological strength not weakness.

concepts.label: basic emotions (Ekman)
concepts.gloss: Ekman's evolved-for-adaptive-value emotions: anger, fear, disgust, surprise, joy, sadness, contempt (Fig. 1.5); critiqued as decontextualizing reduction.

concepts.label: Facial Action Coding System (FACS)
concepts.gloss: Ekman's coding infrastructure for facial expression, mobilized in cognitive neuroscience to correlate brain activity with stimulus photographs.

concepts.label: emotionally competent object
concepts.gloss: Damasio/Ekman category: stimulus (e.g. snake, attractive food) that triggers a basic-emotion response; Gross contests via Happy Meal counterexample.

concepts.label: complex states of mind
concepts.gloss: Darwin's term (E 260) for emotions not revealed by fixed expression — envy, jealousy, suspicion, conceit etc.; require literary not photographic evidence.

concepts.label: affective commitment (Ekman)
concepts.gloss: Ekman's relabel for love/hatred/envy/jealousy — long-duration with named cast of characters — used to expel them from 'emotions' proper.

concepts.label: Cognitive Approaches to Literature (CAL)
concepts.gloss: Subfield (Howard, Crane, Thrailkill, Keen, Zunshine) importing Ekman-Damasio-LeDoux into literary criticism; treated as Trojan horse for impoverished Darwinianism.

concepts.label: brain-body-world nexus
concepts.gloss: Gross's situated alternative to brain-centric cognition; consciousness located across the triad, with the 'world' irreducibly rhetorical.

concepts.label: the New Phrenology
concepts.gloss: Alva Noé's polemical heading (Out of Our Heads) — brain-imaging localization research repeats nineteenth-century phrenological localization errors.

concepts.label: extended emotion
concepts.gloss: Chalmers/Clark Supersizing-the-Mind extension to affect: 'one's environment is always nudging one toward happiness or sadness'; Gross radicalizes via Darwin.

concepts.label: skillfully given accessory
concepts.gloss: Darwin E 22: visual-art components (sea serpent in Laocoön, the two sons) that carry emotional load impossible to read from face alone; Warburg's bewegtes Beiwerk analogue (n.19).

concepts.label: litotes / double negation
concepts.gloss: Affirmative through negation of contrary (Horn 303); Austen 'no unhappy reverie' ≠ 'happy reverie'; Maxim-of-Manner-violation flags stereotype-exceeding situation.

concepts.label: sentimental commerce
concepts.gloss: Sterne's term (Sentimental Journey 9): being-out-of-place produces imbalanced exchange; sentiment as social-transaction not natural immediacy.

concepts.label: indeterminacy (built-in)
concepts.gloss: Griffiths-Scarantino: indeterminacy must be in-built for emotional phenomena to emerge; Roughgarden biodiversity-portfolio argument as biological complement.

concepts.label: interpretive imagination (Darwin)
concepts.gloss: Darwin E 21: viewer 'easily misguided by imagination' once text is read alongside image — methodological self-awareness about word-image interpretation.

concepts.label: rhetorical model of cognition
concepts.gloss: Gross's signature alternative to cognitive-reductionist models; cognition situated in brain-body-world via discursive/rhetorical practices.

concepts.label: impoverished Darwinianism
concepts.gloss: Gross's diagnostic label for the Ekman-Damasio reception of Darwin's Expression — strips out interpretive openness, retains only the basic-emotion image-set methodology.

concepts.label: Maxim of Manner (Grice)
concepts.gloss: Be perspicuous; avoid obscurity and ambiguity; brevity, order. Violation by litotes signals 'getting at something else altogether' (Horn). Imported as analytic lever for Austen-negation.

concepts.label: literary Darwinism (Pinker/Carroll)
concepts.gloss: Cheesecake-for-the-mind thesis — novelistic emotion as virtual training for real-world avoidance; Gross critiques (chapter 4 forward-reference); Sterne-peasants passage cuts against this view.

concepts.label: second-order discomfort (reader)
concepts.gloss: When the narrator pseudo-resolves a character's discomfort diegetically, the reader registers irony and is recruited into a higher-order uncomfortable situation — bridges to volume's titular concept.

concepts.label: civilization as emotional regime
concepts.gloss: Darwin E 217-218: kneeling-with-joined-palms not innate; 'feelings we should now rank as devotional' did not affect 'uncivilized' hearts — historicizes universal-emotion claims via Wedgwood's dare-manus etymology.

concepts.label: biodiversity-as-balanced-portfolio (Roughgarden)
concepts.gloss: Evolution's Rainbow: sexual selection rebalances a species' genetic portfolio across wide-but-not-indefinite behavioral range; supports semiotic-indeterminacy-as-adaptive.

positions.label: Darwin-as-rhetorician thesis
positions.gloss: Gross's titular wager: Darwin's Expression foregrounds inherent rhetoricity of emotion — medium, occasion, social situation — and is thereby a humanistic resource, not (as Ekman has it) a forerunner of decontextualized basic-emotions science.

positions.label: Ekman as strawman / impoverished Darwinianism
positions.gloss: The Ekman tradition has hijacked Darwin: basic-emotion list + FACS + Pictures of Facial Affect set methodologically betray Darwin's own caveats on imagination, mediation, and complex states of mind.

positions.label: love-and-devotion exclusion thesis
positions.gloss: Ekman's basic list excludes love, sympathy, hatred, suspicion, envy, jealousy, avarice, revenge, deceit, devotion etc.; Darwin treats these as central data, with kneeling-in-prayer (devotion) and maternal love (E 82) as cruxes proving emotions need not have fixed expression.

positions.label: complex-states-of-mind argument
positions.gloss: Darwin E 260: many feelings are 'sufficiently distinct' yet not 'revealed by any fixed expression'; the move forces the science of emotion into literary-interpretive territory (Shakespeare on envy/jealousy; Spenser on suspicion).

positions.label: Shakespeare-Spenser literary-humanities turn
positions.gloss: Darwin himself cites Shakespeare ('lean-faced in her loathsome ease' for envy; 'the green-eyed monster' for jealousy) and Spenser ('foul ill-favoured, and grim' for suspicion); the literary corpus is evidence-base not ornament.

positions.label: rhetorical model of cognition (signature)
positions.gloss: Against both brain-localization reductionism and pure-discourse constructionism: cognition is situated in the brain-body-world nexus with the world as irreducibly rhetorical/discursive.

positions.label: anti-CAL polemic
positions.gloss: Howard, Crane, Thrailkill, Keen and Zunshine import Ekman-Damasio infrastructure into literary studies; despite local sensitivity, the underlying impoverished model produces diminishing returns and forecloses cultural-rhetorical analysis.

positions.label: negation as rhetorical operator
positions.gloss: Sterne 'fear not, envied not' and Austen 'no unhappy reverie' (Emma 321) show negation as flouting-of-Gricean-Manner to flag non-stereotypic situations — load-bearing for reading sentimental literature.

positions.label: uncomfortable situatedness (volume's titular crystallization)
positions.gloss: Cognition 'practically situated but uncomfortably so': neither comfortably embedded (EM theory) nor detached (CAL); discomfort recruits author/reader/audience into the emotional phenomenon — this is where 'uncomfortable situations' (the book's title) enters explicitly.

positions.label: indeterminacy-as-adaptive (Roughgarden)
positions.gloss: Against the evolutionary-biology objection (would not transparent-emotion-display be adaptive?): semiotic indeterminacy is the corollate of biodiversity; the work of triangulating 'is never done nor should it be'.

figures.caption_paraphrase: Chimpanzee disappointed and sulky. Drawn from life by Mr. Wood. From Darwin, Expression (1872), p. 139. Wellcome Library CC BY 4.0. Opens the chapter as Darwin's continuity-across-species exhibit.

Horror and Agony. Copied from a photograph by Dr. Duchenne. Darwin Expression p. 307. Long French-language caption (Duchenne 1862) translating to 'an expression of terror mixed with extreme pain... the expression of the damned' (Cuthbertson trans. 1990, p. 92).

Two stacked images. Top: Oscar Gustav Rejlander photograph of 'astonishment' (also in first edition). Bottom: a Duchenne photograph shown to twenty-four persons without explanation — twenty answered 'intense fright' or 'horror', three said pain, one extreme discomfort. From Darwin Expression p. 299.
The uncropped Duchenne photograph (companion to Fig. 1.2). Wellcome Library CC BY 4.0. Demonstrates the staging/framing operations cropping conceals.

Ekman's initial basic-emotion face set: left to right — anger, fear, disgust, surprise, joy, sadness, and Ekman himself as contempt. Reproduced with permission from Paul Ekman Group, LLC. The chapter's primary Ekman exhibit.

Laocoön and Sons (first-century Hellenistic marble group). Photograph by Livio Andronico, CC BY-SA 4.0. Variously read by Virgil ('bellowing'), Winckelmann ('noble'), Lessing ('groaning'), Charles Bell ('silently struggling').

Sir Charles Bell, [sketch from] The Anatomy and Philosophy of [Expression as Connected with the Fine Arts]. Wellcome Library CC BY 4.0. Bell's polemical-foil text that Darwin uses to invoke Lessing on dispersal of violent emotion in visual arts.

Triptych. Left: Photograph 1 in a sequence of smile intensities (PF1-6) from the Pictures of Facial Affect (POFA) Collection, Paul Ekman Group LLC. Center: General Happy Meal Box. Right: 'Joystick black red petri' (digital image by Ansgar Hellwig, PhD). Gross's countermodel triad — face vs. commodified social transaction vs. arbitrary trigger-object.

Weeping Children from Darwin's Expression of Emotions. Wellcome Library CC BY 4.0. The 'mental distress' infant — best known as Ginx's Baby (cf. Prodger, Darwin's Camera 125 / n.52); not a true photograph but a drawing made to look photographic, with Rejlander's 'corrections' (padded chair etc.).

darwin_loci.topic: Lips of young orangs and chimpanzees protruded; sulky chimpanzee + orange withheld; opening passage.
Duchenne galvanism + showing photographs without explanation to twenty educated persons — Darwin's foundational method passage cited by Ekman in 1998 commentary.
Imagination caveat: 'how easily we may be misguided by our imagination' — Darwin's methodological self-awareness on the word-image interpretive loop.
Devotion passage: kneeling-with-joined-palms not innate; Hensleigh Wedgwood etymology (dare manus / Latin) — captive offering hands to be bound; civilization as distinct emotional regime.
Maternal love crux: 'No emotion is stronger than maternal love' yet a mother 'may feel deepest love for her helpless infant, and yet not show it any outward sign'.

Complex states of mind passage with Shakespeare envy ('lean-faced in her loathsome ease'; 'green-eyed monster' for jealousy) and Spenser suspicion ('foul ill-favoured, and grim'); 'guided in a much greater degree than we suppose by our previous knowledge'.
Hatred passage: wilful injury, expecting to suffer, slave thinking about cruel master, savage about bloodthirsty malignant deity — Aristotelian cast-of-characters analysis.
Ekman's 'display rules' citation (located at E 383 in Darwin's text per Gross's reference).
Skillfully-given-accessories passage: visual-arts emotion told by accessories, both human and nonhuman, animate and inanimate, foregrounded and backgrounded.
Ekman afterword 'Universality of Emotional Expression? A Personal History of the Dispute' — disgust-as-model-for-all-emotions passage (n.18).
Darwin footnotes Lessing's Laocoön (per Gross's n.33).
Darwin on infant displaying mental distress — hungry, sleepy, gassy as candidate readings; closing image as locus of constitutive indeterminacy.

neuroscience_loci.topic: Ekman's hands-on annotation of Darwin's method passage; 'Darwin is rarely cited as the first to use it.'
Affective-commitments relabel: 'Emotions are brief and episodic, lasting seconds or minutes' — parental/romantic love, hatred, envy, jealousy excluded on duration + cast-of-characters criterion.

Amygdala-trustworthiness-approachability experiment (n.11); summarized in Damasio Feeling of What Happens.

tensions.label: Darwin-as-rhetorician vs. Darwin-as-proto-Ekman
tensions.gloss: The chapter's animating polemic: does Darwin's photographic-illustration method underwrite (Ekman) a decontextualized basic-emotion science, or (Gross) a rhetorical-interpretive science with interpretive caveats baked in (E 21, E 260)?

tensions.label: Basic emotions vs. complex states of mind
tensions.gloss: Ekman's adaptive-value basic-list vs. Darwin's complex-states-of-mind category (E 260): the latter resists fixed expression and forces literary-humanistic methodology.

tensions.label: Ekman 'affective commitment' relabel vs. Aristotelian cast-of-characters emotion
tensions.gloss: Ekman expels love/hatred/envy/jealousy from 'emotions' on duration+cast-of-characters criteria; Darwin's hatred passage (E 234) and Aristotle's Rhetoric II treat exactly cast-of-characters specification as constitutive — same criterion, opposite valence.

tensions.label: Cognitive-Approaches-to-Literature local sensitivity vs. impoverished foundational model
tensions.gloss: Crane, Thrailkill, Keen, Zunshine produce locally interesting readings while their Ekman-Damasio-LeDoux scaffolding methodologically undercuts cultural-rhetorical analysis (Crane 'home in Comedy of Errors' as exemplar).

tensions.label: Berlant's compassionate-conservatism critique vs. apparently apolitical literary cognitivism
tensions.gloss: Even unintentional reduction of emotion-to-the-face replicates the institutional move Berlant tracks in compassionate-conservatism (Compassion intro): face-to-face encounters substituted for living wage / public education / affordable housing / universal access.

tensions.label: EM-theory comfortable embedding vs. uncomfortable situatedness
tensions.gloss: Dreyfus/Chalmers/Clark/Wheeler/Thompson/Noé extended-mind program treats embedding as resolution; Gross argues cognition is 'practically situated but uncomfortably so' — the volume's titular wedge between EM-theory and CAL.

tensions.label: Logical-symmetry-of-negation (Russell) vs. rhetorical-asymmetry-of-negation (Horn)
tensions.gloss: Russell: 'no not' needed; Horn: litotes carries Q-based-implicature signaling stereotype-violation. The asymmetry is exactly what reading Sterne and Austen requires.

cross_pipeline_bridges.rationale: Same author. Chapter's anti-Ekman polemic operationalizes the 2005 rhetorical-ontology thesis on Darwin's specific 1872 text; Damasio-critique cross-reference at n.11 explicitly cites Secret History of Emotion 21-50.
Hatred passage (E 234) treated as Aristotelian cast-of-characters specification; Aristotle indexed on p.40, 41, 47 — present as background in this chapter as well as Ch.4.
The Emma 'no unhappy reverie' passage (Emma p.321) is the explicit Ch.1→Ch.4 bridge: 'That's one function of negation as we will see in Austen as well' (PDF 56).
Noé's 'In the Beginning Was the Situation' and brain-body-world nexus framework anticipates Ch.3's affordance-theoretic apparatus.

note: Continuous prose. Phase 2 confirmed: Darwin's Expression is Gross's evidence-base AND polemical-target; the Ekman strawman is explicit; the Shakespeare/Spenser passages anchor the literary-humanities turn at E 260; Sterne's peasants passage + Austen's Emma double-negative anchor the negation-as-rhetorical-operator section (a bridge to Ch.4). Bell's Anatomy (Fig. 1.7) and Duchenne's Mécanisme (Fig. 1.2/1.4) are the chapter's two principal non-Darwin primary sources from the visual-arts side. The closing biology-of-indeterminacy argument relies on Roughgarden's Evolution's Rainbow.
